issues.description: Collapsing 'working' and 'walking' states may break cycle detection in push()
issues.detail: All six reviewers flagged that merging the two intermediate states removes the distinction between an ancestor currently expanding its children and a node pending post-visit. push()'s cycle-detection branch now fires for any in-progress node, which may misidentify already-yielded-but-not-yet-marked-sorted nodes as cycles, or weaken real cycle detection. Needs verification and tests.

issues.description: Moving s.state[k] = sorted inside the yield branch changes state-transition semantics
issues.detail: Previously sorted was set unconditionally after pop; now it is only written when state != sorted and yield is invoked. Combined with the walking/working collapse, this leaves a window where a popped node remains 'walking' until successful yield, potentially altering push() behavior on revisits. Reviewers consider it likely correct but want confirmation.

issues.description: No regression test added for the state-reuse bug being fixed
issues.detail: The PR title explicitly claims to fix Sorter state reuse and non-zero stack residue, yet the diff contains no test changes. A test calling Sort() twice on the same Sorter (with overlapping graphs and after a yield=false early termination) would lock in the fix and prevent silent regression. All six reviewers flagged this.

issues.description: Typos in updated comment: 'visisted' and 'if its'
issues.detail: The rewritten comment block introduces 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its' (should be "it's"). Trivial to fix while the comment is already being touched. Flagged by all six reviewers.

issues.description: Document the GC rationale for clear(s.stack) before reslicing
issues.detail: clear(s.stack) followed by s.stack[:0] is intentional — the clear drops references in the backing array so GC can reclaim Node pointers, while the reslice resets length. Without a brief comment explaining this, a future 'cleanup' pass could remove the clear as redundant. Worth a one-line note.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR correctly addresses a real state-reuse bug — the old s.stack[0:] was a no-op leaving stale stack contents — by moving cleanup into a deferred clear+reslice block. The dominant concern is semantic: collapsing 'working' and 'walking' into a single state, combined with delaying the sorted transition until after yield, may subtly alter cycle detection in push(). No regression test accompanies a fix that is specifically about reuse semantics, and the rewritten comment introduces two typos. No P0 blockers; primarily P1 verification work and small polish before merge.
